questions.question: A student wants a poem to evoke a specific place. Which planning choice is most useful?
choices: List precise sensory details and associations connected to that place
Choose a rhyme scheme before deciding what the poem is about
Use abstract words only
Avoid selecting a speaker

questions.question: Which line uses a concrete image rather than an abstract statement?
choices: The day felt difficult
Rain ticks against the rusted fire escape
Hope is important to everyone
Things can change over time

questions.question: A poet repeats 'I remember' at the start of several lines. What is a likely craft purpose?
choices: Replace the need for images
Make the poem's speaker disappear
Create emphasis and a recognizable rhythm
Guarantee an exact rhyme scheme

questions.question: Which revision best strengthens a vague line, 'The room was bad'?
choices: The room was very, very bad
It was not a good room
The room was a room
The sour lamp buzzed above the peeling wallpaper

questions.question: What is the strongest reason to choose a deliberate speaker for a poem?
choices: The speaker shapes what the reader notices and how events are presented
Every poem must be narrated by its author
A speaker determines the number of stanzas
The speaker removes the need for a central idea

questions.question: A poem has strong images but its lines all sound alike. Which revision could improve its movement?
choices: Add unrelated facts to every stanza
Vary line length and sentence structure to fit the poem's pace
Make every line the same length
Remove all punctuation and images

questions.question: Which choice is an example of personification?
choices: The clock was round and white
The clock showed three o'clock
The impatient clock swallowed the afternoon
The clock stood on the shelf

questions.question: A student wants a repeated line to gain meaning each time it returns. What should change across the poem?
choices: The repeated line must change its rhyme each time
The poem must switch to prose
Every stanza should introduce a new speaker
The surrounding context should develop or complicate the repeated line

questions.question: What does enjambment do?
choices: Carries a sentence or phrase across a line break without a full stop
Repeats the first stanza at the end
Makes two line endings rhyme
Names the poem's speaker

questions.question: Which drafting strategy is most useful when a poem feels forced by rhyme?
choices: Keep any word that rhymes, even if it changes the idea
Revise the image or line so meaning leads and sound supports it
Add extra adjectives to every line
Remove the poem's subject

questions.question: A poem's central idea is loneliness, but the images show crowded rooms and unanswered messages. What can the writer improve?
choices: Add a second unrelated theme in every line
Remove all specific details
Connect the chosen images more deliberately to the central idea
Replace the images with a plot summary

questions.question: Which line best uses a metaphor?
choices: Memory is like a drawer
I remembered the drawer
The drawer was beside the desk
Memory is a drawer that will not stay shut

questions.question: Why read a draft aloud during revision?
choices: To hear rhythm, awkward phrasing, repetition, and pauses
To determine the author's grade
To make every line rhyme
To avoid considering the poem's meaning

questions.question: Which revision reduces a cliché while preserving the idea of nervousness?
choices: I was nervous as a cat
My hands worried the paper into soft folds
I had butterflies in my stomach
I was scared stiff

questions.question: A writer uses a sonnet form. What should the form contribute to the poem?
choices: A guarantee that each line has the same subject
A replacement for imagery
A structure that supports the poem's development or creates meaningful constraints
A requirement that the poem explain its theme directly

questions.question: What is a useful role for a title in a poem?
choices: Summarize every image in order
Provide the poem's only sound device
Replace the opening line
Offer a frame or clue that gains significance after reading

questions.question: A poet wants a quiet, reflective mood. Which sound choice is most likely to support it?
choices: Measured phrasing and softer sounds that fit the selected images
A stream of abrupt commands unrelated to the scene
Only capital letters
A rapid list of loud sound effects

questions.question: Which question is most useful in peer feedback on a poem draft?
choices: Can you rewrite this in your own style?
Which image or line stayed with you, and what in the text caused that effect?
Why didn't you make every line rhyme?
Can you remove the speaker?

questions.question: What should a poet check when revising line breaks?
choices: Whether every line contains exactly eight words
Whether each break occurs after a comma
Where breaks create emphasis, pause, surprise, or multiple readings
Whether line breaks match the page margin only

questions.question: A final stanza introduces an image from the opening but changes its context. What can this create?
choices: A new rhyme scheme by itself
An error that must be removed
A switch from poem to essay
A sense of development or closure through a changed perspective
